standard_prerequisites.name: The sheaf of relative differentials picture of a derivation: an S-derivation of a sheaf of O_X-modules F is an R-linear map on sections satisfying the Leibniz rule, and it is determined by its values on a basis of opens
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at statement lines 6410-6416 and in the uniqueness argument at proof lines 6421-6423
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the objects being classified and the Leibniz rule that determines the values on standard opens.

standard_prerequisites.name: Structure of sections over a standard open: every element of the sections of O_X over the standard open defined by f is of the form a/f^n, and f acts invertibly on the sections of F over that open
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes the displayed Leibniz identity solvable for D(a/f^n) and hence makes the derivation determined by D on global sections.

core_obligations: Uniqueness: starting from an R-derivation D : A to M, let U be the standard affine open defined by f and use the Leibniz rule to express D(a)|_U in terms of D(f^n)|_U and D(a/f^n), obtaining a formula that determines D(a/f^n) because f acts invertibly on sections over U (proof lines 6419-6427).

Existence: define the value of the sought derivation at a/f^n by the explicit formula (1/f^n)D(a)|_U minus (a/f^{2n})D(f^n)|_U and verify the derivation properties on the basis of standard opens (proof lines 6428-6433).
Conclude that the two constructions are inverse to one another, so that the map from S-derivations of F to R-derivations of the module of global sections is a bijection (proof lines 6433-6435).
proof_roadmap: Prove uniqueness by solving the Leibniz identity for the value on a/f^n over a standard open (proof lines 6419-6427), then prove existence by displaying that value as a formula and checking the derivation axioms on standard opens (proof lines 6428-6435).
difficulty_reason: The statement is a bijection between the S-derivations of a sheaf of O_X-modules on X = Spec(A) and the R-derivations of the module of global sections, for a ring map R to A with S = Spec(R) (statement lines 6408-6417). The counted proof has real content in two places: uniqueness comes from writing a section over a standard open as a/f^n and solving the Leibniz identity for D(a/f^n), using that f acts invertibly on the sections of F over that open (proof lines 6419-6427), and existence is obtained by displaying the value of the derivation explicitly and checking the axioms on a basis of standard opens (proof lines 6428-6433). It is H2: the argument is a local computation on one affine chart rather than a reduction to a cited theorem, but it uses no hypothesis beyond the affine situation, so no H3 claim is made.
